Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
In a directed weighted graph implemented with adjacency lists, the cost of the operation for vertex v equals its out-degree, i.e., the number of outgoing edges from v. The worst possible single operation in the sequence occurs for the vertex with the maximum out-degree.

* For part (a), the worst possible single operation has a cost of |V| − 1, since in a directed graph on |V| vertices (without self-loops), a single vertex can have at most one outgoing edge to each of the other |V| − 1 vertices, making that the maximum possible out-degree for any one vertex.

* For part (b), using aggregate analysis, the total cost across all |V| operations is the sum of the out-degrees of all vertices, which equals |E| (the total number of edges), because each directed edge contributes exactly 1 to the out-degree of its tail. Dividing this total by the number of operations |V|, the average amortized cost per operation is |E| / |V|.
